Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Implement GitHub issue #40, "R1 06: Question library, weekly team health Template, and Pulse editor", in chrisdoc/surveybeat-next. This is production code. You're in your own git worktree. Run `git fetch origin` and branch `t3/r1-06-pulse-editor` from origin/main, which already has slices 01–05 and 14:
- the workspace and an Alchemy stack with `pr-<n>` preview stages;
- AuthKit sign-in;
- People, Teams, Leads, the permission table in `packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts`, and the Organization setting N;
- email sending;
- the privacy suite: `pnpm test:privacy`, the endpoint `privacyRegistry`, and the preview-privacy and e2e jobs.

## Read first
- `gh issue view 40 --comments` is binding.
- The R1 scope decision: `gh issue view 2 --comments` (question types, the single Template, editing rules).
- GLOSSARY.md (Question, Question version, Dimension, Template, Pulse, Distribution, Anonymity mode, Minimum group size), docs/adr/0004, 0007, 0008, docs/infra.md.
- The existing domain code in `packages/domain/src/people/` and the Organization DO in `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts`, to follow the same patterns: pure decide/apply rules, the DO transaction, SqlDirectory-style storage, and DirectoryHandlers-style API handlers.

## Scope (summary; #40 is binding)
- **Question types:**
  - rating 1–5 with labelled ends, plus an optional "Want to say more?" comment;
  - single choice;
  - long text (≤ 1,000 characters).

  The type is an open union (a Schema TaggedUnion), so eNPS and multiple choice can be added later.
- **Question and Question version are both modelled.** Answers will point at a version. In R1 each Question has exactly one version, and a Question that has Answers can't be edited. Expose an `hasAnswers` check now; it always returns false until slice 09.
- **The weekly team health Template**, with the Dimensions workload, psychological safety, clarity and recognition. Write sensible, short, neutral Question texts, about 5–6 questions, with at least the first one a rating. The Template lives in code.
- **The Pulse editor:**
  - create a Pulse for a Team from the Template;
  - add Questions (from the Template, or new ones);
  - remove and reorder Questions;
  - show the estimated answer time;
  - warn when there are more than 7 Questions or the answer time goes over about 90 seconds;
  - note that one-tap answering needs a rating Question first.
- **Pulse settings:**
  - the Team;
  - the weekly day and time, between 06:00 and 21:00 local;
  - an answer window of 1–6 days, default 3;
  - 0–2 reminders, default 1;
  - anonymous mode only;
  - Invitation Distribution only.

  Model Distribution and Anonymity mode as fields with one allowed value each.
- A warning, not a block, when the Team has fewer members than N.
- **Who may do what:** the permission table decides. Leads and admins of that Team may create and edit its Pulses. Add these actions to `PERMISSIONS` with table tests.
- **Storage:** in the Organization DO, with a new migration.
- **Endpoints:** add the API endpoints and classify every one in `privacyRegistry`. None of them returns Result data.
- **Web:** minimal screens using the message catalog, Tailwind and Base UI: a Pulse list per Team and the Pulse editor.
- **Out of scope:** Rounds, scheduling and sending, which are slice 07.

## Tests
- Domain tests for the editor rules and the Question version invariant.
- Permission table entries.
- API tests per role.
- Extend the e2e where it's cheap.
- No `any`, and no `as` outside tests.
- Exact version pins. Respect pnpm's minimumReleaseAge and never add minimumReleaseAgeExclude.

## Validation
All of these pass: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `typecheck`, `typecheck:effect`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, `test:privacy`.

## Shipping
- Commit on `t3/r1-06-pulse-editor`. The message ends with:
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- Push and open a PR to main titled "R1 06: Question library, Template, and Pulse editor". The body says "Closes #40. Part of #34.", lists the changes and the decisions (the Template's questions, how the time estimate is computed), and ends with:
  `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`
- Don't merge.
- Last line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

## Resolution: Release 1 scope

Decided in a grilling session on 2026-11-07. Later tickets build against this list.

**In Release 1**

- **Question types:** rating (1–5, labeled ends), single choice, long text, and the optional "Want to say more?" comment on rating Questions. The Question type stays an open union.
- **Comments:** the Lead sees them only when the Round meets the minimum group size, after rule-based redaction (names from the Organization's roster, email addresses, phone numbers). The answer page says what the Lead will see. Members see no comments in R1. Recorded as ADR 0001 (`docs/adr/0001-r1-comments-rule-based-redaction.md`, on branch `t3/wayfinder-issue-1`).
- **Templates:** one Template, weekly team health, with Questions grouped into Dimensions (workload, psychological safety, clarity, recognition).
- **Changing Questions:** a Lead can remove, reorder, and add Questions (from the Template or newly written, which creates the first Question version). A Question that has Answers cannot be edited. Question version is modelled from day one, with exactly one version per Question in R1. The pulse editor shows an estimated answer time and warns above 7 Questions or about 90 seconds.
- **Distribution:** Invitation only. Distribution is modelled and fixed per Pulse.
- **Cadence:** weekly only, at a day and time in each member's local time zone. Cadence is modelled so other rules can be added later.
- **Lead controls:** skip a Scheduled Round, pause and resume a Pulse, close an Open Round early, cancel an Open Round.
- **Answer window and reminders:** the answer window is 1–6 days (default 3). The Lead picks 0, 1, or 2 reminders (default 1) at fixed points in the window. Reminders go only to members without a Participation record.
- **Reminder opt-out:** a one-click POST (RFC 8058, List-Unsubscribe) applies per Person per Pulse. Members cannot opt out of Invitations; the Lead ends the Membership instead.
- **Anonymity mode:** anonymous only. The field exists with one allowed value.
- **Changing a Submission:** members can change answers until the Round closes, via the Edit key. This uses the same mechanism as the one-tap flow.
- **Member view of Results:** after AuthKit sign-in, members see the same Results page as the Lead, without comments. In R1, Ready moves straight to Shared; both states stay in the model. A results-ready email goes to the Lead and members. Answering never needs sign-in; viewing Results always does.
- **Actions:** only the Lead creates Actions, from a Result. Each Action has a title, an owner (a Person in the Team), an optional due date, a link to the Result, and an optional Dimension. Statuses are committed, done, and dropped. Proposed is modelled but unused.
- **Where Actions appear:** the next Invitation email and the thank-you screen, at most three: those still committed, plus those marked done since the previous Round.
- **Organization shape:** several Teams with no nesting. Roles are lead and member; viewer is modelled but unused. Each Pulse belongs to one Team, and there are no cross-Team views.

**Not in Release 1:** eNPS, multiple choice, short text, the typo-vs-meaning Question editor, the onboarding, sprint retro, and manager feedback Templates, shared-link Distribution, cadences other than weekly, one-off surveys, attributed and confidential modes, member-proposed Actions, Action follow-up questions, the member's private history page, delayed sharing, and Team nesting and the viewer role.

**Flag for later:** the manager feedback Template scores one Person (the Lead), which is close to SPEC §9. Raise it as a scope question before it is scheduled.

--

# SurveyBeat

Cloudflare-only Effect app. One Durable Object per Organization is the system of record; D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content. Two Workers serve the app/API (`MainWorker`) and the answer page's submission path (`SubmissionWorker`).

Read `SPEC.md` (authoritative spec), `GLOSSARY.md` (domain vocabulary), and `docs/adr/` (binding decisions) before changing behavior. `docs/infra.md` covers stages, WorkOS sign-in, email, and observability.

## Ground rules

- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the React app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*` or Alchemy, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, and `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST` in the environment.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

# A one-tap rating link only preselects; the answer is saved when the member confirms it

SPEC §5.1 said each rating link in an email "records the answer". Email security scanners (Microsoft Defender runs headless Chrome) fetch every link, so recording on GET would count scanners as voters. Some scanners can also produce trusted events, so saving on any interaction would still be unsafe. A rating link (`/a#t=<token>&v=<1–5>`) therefore opens the answer page with that value preselected and writes nothing. The answer is saved only when the member taps "Save and continue", which sits directly under the anonymity statement, or changes the value. A member who taps in the email and leaves without touching the page loses that answer. We accept that loss as the price of never counting a scanner.

## Consequences

- The token exchange that loads the page has no side effects, so R1 has no open tracking at all.
- The anonymity statement is always read before the first Answer is stored.
- One-tap needs a rating Question first in the Pulse. Otherwise the email offers only "Open check-in".
# Workspace layout and toolchain: pnpm, TypeScript 7, oxc tools, and Alchemy v2's Effect runtime kept inside the adapters

**Workspace.** pnpm workspaces with a `catalog:` of exact pins, on Node 24 LTS (`.node-version`). Pinned at: `effect` and all `@effect/*` 4.1.2, `alchemy` and `@alchemy.run/*` 2.0.0-beta.85, `typescript` 7.0.2, and exact `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` versions. The Effect and Alchemy pins move only together, in a PR of their own, because both are marked unstable or beta.

**Packages.**

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/domain` | Schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `pulses/`, `rounds/`, `answering/`, `results/`, `actions/`, `privacy/`), schedule and Result calculations | `effect` only |
| `packages/api` | The HttpApi declaration shared by server and client | `domain` |
| `packages/cloudflare` | Adapters (Organization DO, D1, Queue consumer, `EmailSender`, alarm scheduler) and the two Worker entries: the main Worker and the Submission Worker | `domain`, `api`, `emails` (the Queue consumer renders email), Alchemy runtime |
| `apps/web` | One Vite 8 project with two entries: the app (React, TanStack Router, Base UI) and the answer page (no React, no HttpApi client: plain `fetch` plus shared Schemas) | `api`, `domain` (Schemas) |
| `packages/emails` | Email templates | `domain` |
| `infra` | The Alchemy stack and stages (`pr-<n>`, `staging`, `production`) | everything |

**Cloudflare runtime.** Workers, the Durable Object, the Queue consumer, and Cron are defined with Alchemy v2's Effect runtime, but only in `packages/cloudflare`. If the beta fails us, replacing it with a hand-written bridge of about 100 lines touches only that package.

**Tooling.**
- TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler) with `tsc -b` and project references. Settings: `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
- `@effect/tsgo` provides Effect diagnostics.
- oxfmt formats. oxlint lints, with type-aware rules from `oxlint-tsgolint`.
- A local `jsPlugins` package, `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat`, bans `cloudflare:*` and Alchemy imports in `domain` and `api`, and holds the privacy query lint (no `rowid`, no unordered reads of anonymous tables, no joins between anonymous tables and Participation or Invitation).
- The boundary is also enforced by dependencies: `domain` declares only `effect` and uses `types: []`.

**Tests.** Vitest with `@effect/vitest` everywhere:
- domain and API tests in plain Node with in-memory layers and `HttpApiTest`;
- adapter tests through `@alchemy.run/test` `Test.make({ dev: true })` on local workerd;
- smoke tests with `Test.make()` on the PR stage;
- Playwright end-to-end tests on the PR stage.

`vitest-pool-workers` is not used, and there is no hand-edited wrangler config.

**Answer entry (measured in the answer-page prototype, 2026-11-07).** The answer entry is prerendered static HTML with inline CSS and a small plain TypeScript controller, with no React, Preact, or Base UI. Measured with Lighthouse mobile (slow 4G, 4× CPU), the time until the Question text appears was 1.12 s with this approach, 1.35 s with Preact, 1.61 s with React, and 1.90 s with React plus Base UI. The token request starts from an inline script in `<head>`, and Effect Schema (23.5 KB gzip) loads after first paint. Budget: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip on the critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB, 1 request before first paint and 2 before the Question text. A Lighthouse CI gate checks FCP ≤ 800 ms, LCP ≤ 1.3 s, and TBT ≤ 50 ms.

## Considered Options

- **TypeScript 5.9 or 6.** Rejected: 7.0.2 is npm `latest`, Effect recommends it, and Alchemy is built against it. 6.0 is the end of the JavaScript-based compiler line. Our tools (oxc, Vite/rolldown, Vitest) don't depend on the old compiler API.
- **Biome, or ESLint with Prettier.** Rejected in favour of oxlint and oxfmt. oxlint's `jsPlugins` let the boundary and privacy rules be ordinary lint rules, and `oxlint-tsgolint` gives type-aware rules on TypeScript 7.
- **A hand-written Effect bridge from day one.** Deferred: Alchemy's runtime removes the bridge code. Keeping it in one package makes the switch cheap if we need it.

## Consequences

A spike on a preview stage verifies this before the walking skeleton is built. It checks the Organization DO with `SqliteClient`, transactions, migrations, and an alarm, a Queue consumer with a dead-letter queue, the Submission Worker with every log setting off, the deployed cold start, and `tsc -b` with project references on TypeScript 7.0.2.

## 5. Functional requirements

Requirements are grouped by the loop step they serve. Section 8 sequences them into releases.

### 5.1 Ask: set up and send pulses

- A lead can create a pulse in under two minutes by starting from a template. The product ships with templates for weekly team health, sprint retrospectives, onboarding check-ins (at 30, 60, and 90 days), and a manager feedback round.
- Question types are rating (1 to 5, with labeled ends), eNPS (0 to 10), single choice, multiple choice, short text, and long text. Each rating question can have an optional "Want to say more?" comment field.
- The question library is shared across the organization. Admins can mark questions as standard, so that every team asking the same question produces comparable data across the organization.
- The pulse editor shows an estimated answer time, and warns when a pulse goes over 7 questions or about 90 seconds.
- Optional rotation. A pulse can have a fixed core set of questions plus a rotating set, where each round asks one or two different questions. This covers more topics without making each round longer.
- Cadence uses each member's local time zone. Monday 9:00 means 9:00 for each recipient. A lead can skip a round (for holidays) or pause a pulse.
- Channels are email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Each member picks their preferred channel. Email is the fallback for everyone.
- The first question can be answered directly from the message. In email, each rating value is a link that opens the answer page with that value chosen; the answer is saved when the member confirms it there, because email security scanners open every link (ADR 0007). In Slack and Teams, the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal for the rest.
- Reminders go only to members who have not answered, and there are at most two per round. A member can turn reminders off.
- A shareable link remains available for teams that do not use invitations. A link round cannot compute a response rate and cannot guarantee one answer per person. The UI says so.

### 5.2 Answer: the member experience

- The answer page loads in under one second on a mid-range phone on 4G. It needs no sign-in when opened from an invitation token. It does need sign-in when opened from the shared link, if the organization requires it.
- One question per screen on mobile. All questions on one page on desktop. Keyboard navigation works fully. The page meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
- The answer page states the round's anonymity mode in plain words before the first question, along with what the lead will and will not see. Example: "Your lead sees the team's combined answers once at least 4 people respond. Your name is never stored with your answers."
- A member can change answers until the round closes. In anonymous rounds this needs a design that does not link the person to the submission on the server. The recommended approach is a random edit key that only the member's browser stores. If the member loses the key, they cannot edit, and that is acceptable.
- After submitting, the member sees a thank-you screen and the team's current open actions. This reminds them that answering leads to change.
- A member has a private history page that shows their own past attributed answers. It also shows their anonymous answers if their browser still holds those edit keys. Nobody else can see this page.
- Interface languages at launch are English and German. All strings must be translatable from day one.

### 5.6 Administration

- **Sign-in.** Sign-in uses WorkOS AuthKit, with email magic link, Google, and Microsoft for small teams, and enterprise SSO (SAML or OIDC) for organizations that set it up.
- **Directory sync.** WorkOS Directory Sync (SCIM) creates and removes people and can map directory groups to teams. When a person is removed from the directory, they lose access immediately. Their memberships end on that date, and history stays intact.
- **Roles and permissions.** WorkOS manages organization-level roles (admin, member). Team-level roles (lead, member, viewer) live in SurveyBeat's own data, because they belong to the domain. Permission checks are one function of (person, action, resource), defined in one place and tested as a table.
- **Audit log.** The system records admin and lead actions, such as changing privacy settings, changing anonymity modes, exporting data, and adding leads. Use WorkOS Audit Logs if that fits, or a store inside SurveyBeat.
- **Billing.** Not in the first release. Design the model so that seats or teams per organization can be counted later.

### 5.7 Integrations and API

- **Slack app and Microsoft Teams app.** Members can answer from the messages. Leads get the results summary in a channel they choose. A slash command or message action shows the team's current health.
- **Public API.** A small, versioned HTTP API, authenticated with organization API keys, that returns results and actions. All privacy rules apply.
- **MCP server.** A remote MCP server lets a lead use an AI assistant to ask about their teams' results and manage actions. It enforces the same permissions and privacy thresholds as the web app, because it calls the same domain services.
- **Webhooks.** Webhooks for "round results ready" and "action created or updated".

### 5.8 Product surfaces outside the app

- A marketing landing page, a pricing page that can be a placeholder, and legal pages for privacy, terms, and the data processing agreement. The old app had legal page stubs. The rebuild needs real text before any external customer uses it.
- Transactional emails for invitations, reminders, results-ready notices, and action updates. They must look good in the major email clients and in dark mode.

## 6. Platform and architecture

Everything runs on Cloudflare. No Next.js, no Vercel, and no separate cloud provider for compute or data. WorkOS (identity) and the Slack and Microsoft Teams platforms are the only required external services.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Infrastructure as code | alchemy.run | Every Cloudflare resource, binding, secret, and custom domain is declared in TypeScript with Alchemy. No dashboard changes. No Terraform. No hand-edited wrangler config. |
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers | One Worker serves the API and the static web app (Workers static assets). Add more Workers only when a job needs a different runtime profile, such as a queue consumer. |
| Business logic | Effect | All domain logic, data access, and integrations are Effect programs. Errors, dependencies, retries, and timeouts are typed. Domain services are Effect services with layers that can be swapped in tests. |
